completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed prune_next_body()/count_pruned_next_ids() to preserve a CLI flag segment on a Run line and never silently drop an active task, added 25 new flag-bearing --prune test cases across both roadmap layouts, extended roadmap-format.md's Next Grammar, redeployed, and ran the full gate set (clean except three pre-existing, evidenced, unrelated exclusions: a hanging literature-extension test, a lean doc-lint gap, and a 225B eager-load budget overage).

memory_candidates.content: When embedding a literal single-quote character inside an awk program that is itself passed to awk via a bash single-quoted script string (awk -v x="$y" '...'), the embedded quote breaks the shell's quoting and silently corrupts the script -- there is no error, just wrong output (observed: a literal variable-name placeholder printed instead of its value). Avoid by using a different delimiter (e.g. square brackets) around the interpolated value inside the message, rather than fighting with the '"'"' escape idiom inline in a multi-line awk block. Caught only by a full end-to-end script run against the real file; an isolated scratchpad re-typing of the same awk body can mask this if the re-typed copy happens to use different (correct) quoting.

When segmenting a trailing CLI-flag-like suffix off a comma/space-delimited id list in a Run line (or similar grammar admitting intra-list whitespace, e.g. '716, 714'), anchor the split on the first whitespace-preceded '-' rather than the first run of whitespace. Splitting on the first whitespace mis-splits any grammar-legal intra-list space before the flag segment is reached, creating a second content-loss path distinct from the one being fixed.
